proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(D=Sd\) and work throughout with a regular conditional experiment given \(E_0\).  The compatibility restriction follows before any lower-bound construction is attempted.  For every class member define, only in this proof,
\[
Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0).
\]
By the definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\), and by \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity},
\[
\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Taking traces and then applying Jensen's inequality to the nonnegative random variable \(\|Y\|_2^2\) gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]
=\operatorname{tr}(I_D)=D,
\qquad
D^2
=\{\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]\}^2
\le \mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]
\le B,
\tag{1}
\]
where the last inequality is \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  Thus \(B\ge D^2=(Sd)^2\) is necessary for nonemptiness.  Equality in Jensen at \(B=D^2\) forces \(\|Y\|_2^2=D\) almost surely.  In particular, nonemptiness does not imply the strict slack needed to perturb a common-support donor distribution.

We next give a causal completion used by all applicable channels.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose the event path in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal Z_+\) contained in the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw the bounded historical response paths independently across \((s,i)\), from kernels that may vary with \((s,i)\) and satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=m_s(X_{st}).
\tag{2}
\]
Draw the observed event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\), also independently across units.  Then, with \(\varepsilon_{sti}=Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set observed and historical potential outcomes according to \texttt{ass:consistency} and \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}; make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment and all potential outcomes invariant to other units' assignments.  This verifies \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  Set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Equation (3) verifies the two additional restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Donors are chosen conditionally independently of this panel and identically over \(j\).

For the three non-donor channels and either compatible value \(B\ge D^2\), a common admissible donor law is explicit.  Let \(Y\) be uniform on
\[
\{\pm\sqrt D e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\]
where \((e_k)_{k=1}^D\) is the standard basis, and put \(Z_j=z_0+Y_j\) for conditionally independent copies \(Y_j\).  Direct summation yields
\[
\mathbb E[Y]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[YY^\top]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|Y\|_2^4]=D^2\le B.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the full covariance is \(I_D\), which lies in the declared ellipticity envelope because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), and (4) verifies the fourth-moment condition even at the boundary \(B=D^2\).

We use the elementary binary relative-entropy bound
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le C_\eta v^2
\quad\text{whenever }p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta].
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, the second derivative with respect to the first argument is \(1/\{u(1-u)\}\), so (5) follows from Taylor's theorem on the displayed compact interval.

For the treated channel, use an independent uniform historical design and choose the common regression carrier in the interior of \([0,B]\): take an affine carrier with nonzero standardized slope when \(\lambda\ge1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp when \(0<\lambda<1\).  Fixed rescaling within the nonempty class envelopes verifies \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness} and \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}.  Write
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^S\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\),
\[
|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\le c_0.
\]
Choose fixed baseline event-response probabilities in \([2\eta,1-2\eta]\), and change only the treated event-response probability in cohort \(s\) by \(v_s\).  Taking \(c_0\) sufficiently small keeps all probabilities in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The historical surfaces, donor law (4), and all other observed laws remain fixed.  Absorbing a fixed positive wealth scale into \(c_0\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (5) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)|
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\tag{6}
\]
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_{s=1}^Sn_sv_s^2
=Cc_0^2.
\tag{7}
\]

For the smoothing channel, choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), and set
\[
b=c_b(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}.
\]
For a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump \(\psi\) with \(\psi(0)=1\), perturb only that cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi\!\left(\frac{x-z_{0s_*}}b\right).
\tag{8}
\]
Choose as common carrier an interior-range affine surface with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient if \(\lambda\ge1\), and an interior-range asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp if \(0<\lambda<1\).  Choose it with fixed slack in the Holder and two-sided-modulus envelopes.  For a displacement of Euclidean size \(\delta\), the increment of (8) is at most \(Cc_1\delta^\kappa\): this is the scaled Holder bound for \(\delta\le b\), while for \(\delta>b\) it follows from \(b^\lambda\le C\delta^\kappa\).  Hence a sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves the response range, Holder ball, and both sides of the local-modulus condition.  With independent uniform historical design, the bump support has probability at most \(Cb^d\).  Since \(S\) is fixed, (5) and the maximizing choice imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
&=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\\
&\ge c\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=cR_{\mathrm{sm}},
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}
\le C.
\tag{10}
\]

For the spacing channel, invoke \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  Its rare-active-block construction has design-only geometric mixing, the required marginal density, full-design centering, and the two-sided modulus, and gives
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,\mathrm{sp}},dP_{1,\mathrm{sp}}\}
\ge a_{\mathrm{sp}}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{11}
\]
At \(B=D^2\), use (4) as the common donor marginal in that construction; donors carry no spacing-channel information, so this replacement changes neither affinity nor target separation.  Thus (11) is valid at both compatible envelope values.  Only affinity, not a Kullback--Leibler bound, is asserted in this channel.

It remains to construct the donor channel, for which assume the fixed interior-compatible slack \(B>D^2\).  Choose \(a_0>1\) so close to one that
\[
D^2+D(a_0^2-1)<B.
\tag{12}
\]
Let the coordinates of \(W=(W_1,\ldots,W_D)^\top\) be independent with
\[
P(W_k=a_0)=P(W_k=-a_0)=\frac1{2a_0^2},
\qquad
P(W_k=0)=1-\frac1{a_0^2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Every atom of the finite Cartesian support has positive probability.  Moreover,
\[
\mathbb E[W]=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(W)=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|W\|_2^4]
=Da_0^2+D(D-1)
=D^2+D(a_0^2-1)<B.
\tag{14}
\]
The strict inequality in (14) is precisely where the fixed slack \(B-D^2\) is used.

Choose a coordinate \(k_0\) belonging to a cohort \(s_0\).  For \(|\delta|\) small, alter only the three probabilities of \(W_{k_0}\) to
\[
p_+(\delta)=\frac{1+\delta^2}{2a_0^2}+\frac{\delta}{2a_0},
\quad
p_-(\delta)=\frac{1+\delta^2}{2a_0^2}-\frac{\delta}{2a_0},
\quad
p_0(\delta)=1-\frac{1+\delta^2}{a_0^2}.
\tag{15}
\]
All probabilities remain positive for sufficiently small \(|\delta|\), their sum is one, and
\[
\mathbb E_\delta[W_{k_0}]=\delta,
\qquad
\mathbb E_\delta[W_{k_0}^2]=1+\delta^2,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\delta(W_{k_0})=1.
\tag{16}
\]
Independence of the other centered coordinates therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E_\delta[W]=\delta e_{k_0},
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\delta(W)=I_D.
\tag{17}
\]
Let \(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+c_2N^{-1/2}e_{k_0}\), put \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\), and under law \(\ell\) set \(Z=z^{(0)}+W\) with probabilities (13) for \(\ell=0\) and (15) for \(\ell=1\).  Equations (16)--(17) give the required two means and covariance \(I_D\) on one common finite support.  The map
\[
\delta\longmapsto
\mathbb E_\delta[\|W-\delta e_{k_0}\|_2^4]
\]
is continuous.  By the strict inequality in (14), taking \(c_2\) sufficiently small, with the permitted choice depending on \(B-D^2\), keeps this standardized fourth moment below \(B\) for every \(N\).  Thus covariance and fourth moment remain inside their envelopes.  Taylor expansion of the three-category relative entropy around the interior probability vector (13) yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\delta^2
\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{18}
\]

For \(\kappa=1\), choose the weighted regression carrier to have a nonzero affine slope in direction \(e_{k_0}\).  For \(0<\kappa=\lambda<1\), in cohort \(s_0\) use
\[
x\longmapsto c_3
+c_4|e_{k_0}^\top(x-z_{s_0}^{(0)})|^\lambda
+c_5|e_{k_0}^\top(x-z_{s_0}^{(1)})|^\lambda,
\qquad c_4,c_5>0,quad c_4\ne c_5.
\tag{19}
\]
Fixed rescaling puts the carrier inside the response and Holder envelopes.  At either center, move along the coordinate ray pointing away from the other center.  Both cusp increments then have the same sign, and the cusp centered at the starting point has magnitude \(c_4\delta'^\lambda\) or \(c_5\delta'^\lambda\).  The Holder bound supplies the reverse upper inequality.  Since \(\Sigma=I_D\), this verifies the two-sided standardized modulus at both centers for \(0<\delta'\le\delta_0\).  Evaluation at the two centers gives
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s
\{m_s(z_s^{(1)})-m_s(z_s^{(0)})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{20}
\]
Keep the historical observed law, its surface, and the observed event mean fixed across the donor laws.  Complete the unobserved untreated event outcomes under law \(\ell\) with cohort means \(m_s(z_s^{(\ell)})\).  By \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (20) is a causal-target separation, so
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{don}}}(z_0)-
  \tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{don}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{21}
\]

For completeness, bounded divergence implies positive testing affinity here by an elementary calculation.  Let \(p_1,p_0\) be densities with respect to a common dominating measure, put \(\phi(x)=x\log x\), and let \(A=\{p_1\ge p_0\}\).  Convexity of \(\phi\), applied separately on \(A\) and \(A^c\) with probability measure proportional to \(p_0\), gives
\[
\int p_0\phi(p_1/p_0)
\ge \operatorname{kl}\{P_1(A),P_0(A)\}.
\]
The two Bernoulli probabilities differ by \(\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Taylor expansion of binary relative entropy in its first argument, whose second derivative is at least four, therefore gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)
\ge2\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{22}
\]
Reducing the fixed constants \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (22) uniformly positive in the treated, smoothing, and, when \(B>D^2\), donor channels; (11) supplies spacing affinity.  The constants in the donor channel may depend on the fixed slack \(B-D^2\).  The event path is chosen in \(\mathcal Z_+\) with conditional probability one.  Equations (2)--(4), the channelwise calculations, and the causal completion verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  Thus all four pairs exist when \(B>D^2\), while (4), (6)--(11) give exactly the three asserted pairs when \(B=D^2\).  Equation (1) shows that \(B<D^2\) yields no class member, and no donor-channel converse has been asserted at equality.

Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\},
\]
and first condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N)\).  On each successful fit, the definition of \(a_{sti}\) gives polynomial reproduction:
\[
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
a_{sti}b_r(u_{st})^\top
=e_0^\top G_s^{-1}
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{st}b_r(u_{st})b_r(u_{st})^\top
=e_0^\top.
\tag{23}
\]
Apply (23) to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\).  The Holder remainder from \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness} then gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{24}
\]
After multiplying by \(\pi_s\) and summing over cohorts, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the unit-cluster historical fluctuations
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^Ta_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}, followed by \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N]=0.
\tag{25}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables conditionally independent over \((s,i)\).  Because \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^T|a_{sti}|.
\tag{26}
\]
For a conditionally centered random variable in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of the exponential bounds its moment generating function by the endpoint mixture having the same mean; differentiating the logarithm of that mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{27}
\]
Multiplication of (27) over the independent unit clusters, exponential Markov inequality, and optimization over \(v>0\), repeated for \(-U\), yield
\[
P_P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{28}
\]
The entire calendar history of one unit is one cluster in (28); no temporal outcome independence or mixing is used.

Similarly, define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(V_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence permits adjoining the donors, and cross-unit independence gives conditional independence.  By consistency and \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}, its conditional range length is at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  Applying (27) gives
\[
P_P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{29}
\]
A union bound combines (28)--(29), so dependence between a unit's historical path and event outcome is allowed.

For donor calibration, define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^NY_j,
\qquad D=Sd.
\]
Conditional donor replication gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y_j\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\tag{30}
\]
In the expansion of \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), every term containing a singleton sample index has conditional expectation zero.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings, together with \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}, give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
\]
For the proof event \(\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}\), Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}
=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{32}
\]
Projection onto the cube cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), because \(z_0\) lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds therefore give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\frac{q_N}{\sqrt N}
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
On the good sample, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\).  The upper inequality in \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (33) then show
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa
=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{34}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) be the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N)\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), the interval is \([-B,B]\).  By \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}, each conditional mean contrast in \texttt{def:target} lies in \([-B,B]\), and the positive cohort weights sum to one; hence \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\).  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (24), and (34) decompose the estimation error into the event and historical fluctuations plus two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Therefore noncoverage implies failure of (28) or (29).  Iterated conditioning and (32) yield, for all positive sample sizes,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P_P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{35}
\]
No selector-tail probability enters (35), which proves exact finite-sample conditional coverage.

We next bound expected length.  On successful fits, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})
c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{36}
\]
The support of \(K\) and the same deterministic absolute-weight bound imply
\[
A_L\le C\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\tag{37}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(\lambda\), conditionally on \(E_0\) and \(\widetilde z_s\), and then integrate over the donor sample.  Cauchy--Schwarz over the fixed cohorts gives
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2},
\tag{38}
\]
where \(N^{-\lambda/2}\le N^{-\kappa/2}\) follows from \(N\ge1\) and \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  Since \(D\), \(B\), and \(\alpha\) are fixed, (31) gives \(q_N\le C\), and therefore
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}
\le CN^{-\kappa/2}
=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{39}
\]
The selector lemma gives
\[
\sup_P P_P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)
\le CR_{\star,\beta}
\tag{40}
\]
along the stated arrays; the deterministic condition \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) holds eventually.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), the nonfallback length is at most \(2H_\alpha\), and eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Combining (36)--(40) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{41}
\]
This argument uses only the upper fourth-moment envelope, so it is valid both for \(B>D^2\) and for \(B=D^2\).

It remains to prove the appropriate lower bounds.  Let
\[
\mathcal Q_B=
\begin{cases}
\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\},&B>D^2,\\
\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\},&B=D^2.
\end{cases}
\tag{42}
\]
For every \(q\in\mathcal Q_B\), use the pair from \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}.  The perturbation constants in the treated, smoothing, and donor constructions can be multiplied by a sufficiently small fixed factor: equations (7), (10), and (18) in that lemma's proof then make their affinities arbitrarily close to one by (22), while their target separations retain the same rate with a smaller positive constant.  In the spacing construction, reducing the fixed rare-block activation constant makes the no-active-block probability, and hence affinity, arbitrarily close to one, while multiplying separation only by a fixed positive power of that constant.  Thus, for the fixed \(\alpha<1/2\), all applicable pairs may be chosen with
\[
A_q:=\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\ge2\alpha+a_0
\tag{43}
\]
for a fixed \(a_0>0\), and with target values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) satisfying
\[
|\theta_1-\theta_0|\ge cR_q^{1/2}.
\tag{44}
\]

Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) be the conditional overlap measure.  Uniform honesty and domination of \(\mu_q\) by both laws imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\mid E_0\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\mid E_0\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha
\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{45}
\]
On this event \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Hence (44)--(45) give
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{46}
\]
When \(B>D^2\), maximizing (46) over all four channels yields
\[
c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{47}
\]
When \(B=D^2\), maximizing over the three asserted channels yields only
\[
c_\alpha
\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}

prose_updates.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. Consistency and cohort-average event transport identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw local-polynomial estimator is exactly a cohort-weighted event coefficient. Over the full-design-centered class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), bounded unit response laws may be heterogeneous subject only to a common conditional mean, while geometric beta mixing is imposed on the historical design process alone. Nonemptiness forces the joint wealth and donor fourth-moment envelope to satisfy \(B\ge(Sd)^2\). For fixed interior-compatible \(B>(Sd)^2\), matching bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\); at \(B=(Sd)^2\), the upper bounds and exact finite-sample conditional coverage remain valid, but only the treated, smoothing, and spacing lower channels are claimed. The feasible construction projects the full independent donor mean once, uses one normalized-shape local-polynomial fit per cohort, and combines bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding radii with exact Holder--Taylor and donor-modulus allowances. The log-adjusted spacing term is unavoidable uniformly, and under strict envelope slack the donor channel saturates at \(N^{-1}\) in mean squared error when \(\lambda>1\), conditional on the two-sided local modulus.

project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact cohortwise weighted-panel coefficient representation, exact finite-sample conditional coverage over every nonempty compatible envelope, and matching risk and honest-length frontiers when the standardized donor fourth-moment envelope has fixed strict slack above \((Sd)^2\). At the equality boundary it retains the same feasible upper bounds and the treated, smoothing, and spacing converses without asserting a universal donor converse. A normalized Gram-shape selector under design-only geometric beta mixing, full-data bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding calibration, an exact Taylor allowance, full-sample covariance-standardized donor control, and channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish these results without donor splitting, sequential overlap, a dense-site condition, an upper local-mass condition, or identical unit response laws.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and a standardized fourth-moment envelope; historical training coordinates are exact. Writing \(D=Sd\), nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\), and the donor lower experiment uses fixed strict slack \(B>D^2\); the estimator and interval do not. The full donor mean is projected once onto the proxy cube and feeds one log-adjusted local-polynomial fit per cohort, selected by normalized Gram shape. The finite-sample conditionally honest interval uses the resulting full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event bounded-cluster Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and one full-sample donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared observable bad sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and explain why compounded buy-and-hold wealth requires more than linear return matching; their work informs the event-transport layer rather than supplying this frontier. Barber and Lyon (1997), Mitchell and Stafford (2000), and Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the warning that matching only marginal or mean return paths generally discards within-path dependence needed for compounded wealth. That warning is motivation, not a theorem here and not an observational-equivalence claim under the maintained full wealth panel. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation, Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution, and Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study local-polynomial regression evaluated at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer. Those experiments differ from the exact historical coordinates and single generated event query here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block-coupling template; here dependence is imposed only on the historical design. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for arbitrary relative growth, and Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies without deriving the generated-proxy minimax frontier. The present proof adds one full-donor center, heterogeneous bounded unit-response clusters with a common conditional mean, exact finite-sample conditional coverage, an explicit rare-block spacing witness, and the necessary distinction between strict and boundary donor-moment compatibility.
prose_updates.interpretation: For every integer \(T\ge3\), the replicated-smoothing term obeys \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), where \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\). Hence the active upper risk is exactly \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\): smoothing remains useful bookkeeping but is never uniquely active. For fixed interior-compatible \(B>(Sd)^2\), this is also the matched lower frontier: the oracle region has \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta})\), the generated-proxy region reverses that relation, and the boundary equates the two. The sole donor elbow is \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\). At the compatible moment boundary \(B=(Sd)^2\), the same upper diagram holds but no universal donor converse is claimed, so the generated-proxy phase is not declared minimax-sharp there. The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball or anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality. The risk and honest-length results additionally use the two explicit full-design mean-stability and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence. Geometric beta mixing is required only for the historical design, and bounded unit response paths may otherwise be arbitrarily dependent over time and heterogeneous across units subject to their common conditional mean. Nonemptiness forces \(B\ge(Sd)^2\); the four-channel lower frontier additionally requires fixed strict slack \(B>(Sd)^2\), while exact coverage and upper bounds do not. At equality only the three non-donor lower channels are asserted. The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass. The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp minimax constants.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of event-transport identification, the exact full-donor FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, a log-adjusted selector bound under design-only geometric beta mixing, a positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, compatible causal-panel lower-bound embeddings, a matching conditional-risk and expected-length frontier for fixed \(B>(Sd)^2\), and an exact finite-sample conditionally honest interval over every nonempty compatible envelope. At \(B=(Sd)^2\), the estimator, exact coverage, and upper bounds remain proved, together with treated, smoothing, and spacing lower bounds, but no universal donor converse. Historical and event unit response laws may be heterogeneous and each unit's calendar history is treated as one bounded cluster. No donor splitting, covariance estimation, response-variance lower bound, sequential overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, studentization, or temporal-outcome mixing condition is used. The donor converse remains conditional on both strict envelope slack and the two-sided local modulus, and causal interpretation remains conditional on event transport.
